Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: This file outlines the topics covered in the module, progressing from foundational HTML5 Drag and Drop API concepts and browser compatibility through making elements draggable, handling drag lifecycle events (dragstart, dragover, drop, dragend), working with the DataTransfer object, and implementing practical drag-and-drop interactions; instructors use it to structure lesson sequencing and learners use it as a roadmap of what to expect throughout the module.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: An outline of all topics covered in the module — including the HTML5 Drag and Drop API, draggable elements, and key drag events — giving learners and instructors a navigable overview of the module's scope.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to HTML5 Drag and Drop
Artifacts.Description: A reading that introduces the HTML5 Drag and Drop API, explaining what it is, how browsers support it, and the core concepts behind draggable elements, used by learners to build foundational understanding before writing any code.

Artifacts.Name: Making Elements Draggable
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains how to make HTML elements draggable using the draggable attribute and the native Drag and Drop API, guiding learners through the first practical step of implementing drag-and-drop behaviour in a webpage.

Artifacts.Name: Handling the dragstart Event
Artifacts.Description: A reading that covers the dragstart event in depth — what triggers it, how to use the DataTransfer object to attach data, and how to set visual feedback — teaching learners how to initialise a drag operation correctly.

Artifacts.Name: Handling the dragover Event
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains the dragover event, why calling preventDefault() on it is required to designate a valid drop target, and how to use it as a gatekeeper in drag-and-drop interactions, helping learners enable droppable areas.

Artifacts.Name: Handling the drop Event
Artifacts.Description: A reading that describes the drop event — how to retrieve DataTransfer data, identify the dragged element, and update the DOM to reflect a completed drop — teaching learners how to finalise a drag-and-drop interaction.

Artifacts.Name: Building an Interactive UI Component
Artifacts.Description: A reading that walks learners through constructing a complete drag-and-drop UI component by combining HTML structure, the native API, JavaScript event handling, data-model management, and accessibility considerations into a cohesive example.
